artworks.title: Professor Bert Codman moving his Punch & Judy show

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: Photograph of Fred Tickner (1898-1992) (left) and Bruce Macloud (right) holding versions of Mr. Punch and Clown, standing outside a branch of the tobacconist's Angel Botibil & Company, in London's Leicester Square. Photograph by Howard Marks, labelled 'The Punch and Judy Men Meet'. Taken at an Annual Exhibition of the British Puppet and Model Theatre Guild exhibition, possibly October 1938. Black and white photograph by Hayward Marks. Gerald Morice Collection.

artworks.title: Untitled

artworks.title: Photograph by Lee Miller, 'Saul Steinberg at Farley Farm, Chiddingly, England', from the portfolio 'Quintessential Lee Miller'
artworks.medium: Gelatin silver print on Forte Polywarmtone FB semimatt fibrebase paper, hand printed from Lee Miller's original negatives and selenium-toned.
artworks.description:
Photograph by Lee Miller, 'Saul Steinberg at Farley Farm, Chiddingly, England', from the portfolio 'Quintessential Lee Miller: Six photographs by Lee Miller selected by Mark Haworth-Booth', gelatin silver print, 1952 reprinted 2007.

This unusual group portrait features the American cartoonist and illustrator Saul Steinberg, a friend of Lee Miller, as he wrestles with some garden hose. It forms part of ‘Working Guests’, a tongue-in-cheek article advising how to host the perfect soirée and represents Miller's last major article for British Vogue, published in July 1953. Miller declared that she had 'devoted four years of research and practice to getting all my friends to do all the work'. It features many of Miller’s other friends performing usual tasks around her home, including the artists Dorothea Tanning rewiring a plug and Richard Hamilton repairing some curtains.

artworks.title: Photograph by Lee Miller, 'Hampstead Fair, London, England', from the portfolio 'Quintessential Lee Miller'.
artworks.medium: Gelatin silver print on Forte Polywarmtone FB semimatt fibrebase paper, hand printed from Lee Miller's original negatives and selenium-toned.
artworks.description:
Photograph by Lee Miller, 'Hampstead Fair, London, England', from the portfolio 'Quintessential Lee Miller: Six photographs by Lee Miller selected by Mark Haworth-Booth', gelatin silver print, 1949 reprinted 2007.

Lee Miller applies an experimental and Surrealist perspective to a London fairground at night, photographed after the Second World War had ended. She uses multiple slow exposures, at night, to reveal the lights and frivolity of the world post-war.

artworks.title: Photograph by Lee Miller, 'Bürgermeister of Leipzig's daughter after suicide, Germany', from the portfolio 'Quintessential Lee Miller'.
artworks.medium: Gelatin silver print on Forte Polywarmtone FB semimatt fibrebase paper, hand printed from Lee Miller's original negatives and selenium-toned.
artworks.description:
Content Warning

Photograph by Lee Miller, 'Bürgermeister of Leipzig's daughter after suicide, Germany', from the portfolio 'Quintessential Lee Miller: Six photographs by Lee Miller selected by Mark Haworth-Booth', gelatin silver print, 1945 reprinted 2007.

Lee Miller was one of the only female photojournalists who covered the frontline during WWII. This powerful yet harrowing photograph captures the suicide of Regina Lisso (May 24, 1924 - April 18, 1945) in the Leipzig Town Hall to avoid capture by American soldiers. Lisso was found with her father, Deputy Mayor Dr. Kurt Lisso and her mother Renate Lubbert, as well as other notable military personnel who had all ingest cyanide. The scene of the suicides was extensively photographed by other photographers at the scene, including Robert Capa and Margaret Bourke-White.

This limited-edition selection of six gelatin silver print photographs printed from Lee Miller's original negatives were selected by Mark Haworth-Booth, the curator of the 2007 V&A exhibition The Art of Lee Miller. They have been printed and published by the Lee Miller Archives to commemorate the centenary year of Lee Miller’s birth.

artworks.title: Photograph by Lee Miller, 'Women with fire-masks, Downshire Hill, London, England', from the portfolio 'Quintessential Lee Miller'
artworks.medium: Gelatin silver print on Forte Polywarmtone FB semimatt fibrebase paper, hand printed from Lee Miller's original negatives and selenium-toned. /
artworks.description:
Photograph by Lee Miller, 'Women with fire-masks, Downshire Hill, London, England', from the portfolio 'Quintessential Lee Miller: Six photographs by Lee Miller selected by Mark Haworth-Booth', gelatin silver print, 1941 reprinted 2007.

During the Second World War, Lee Miller often used exterior locations for fashion shoots, particularly when bombing cut off electricity to her studio.  This air raid shelter is situated in the London garden of Miller’s partner, the artist Roland Penrose. The masks are for Air Raid Protection wardens and intended to protect them from incendiary bombs. Miller produced many ‘soft propaganda’ shoots for magazines such as Vogue during WWII. Many focused on women’s contribution to the war effort and included fashion shoots, pattern books and knitwear promoting women’s safety and styling during the war period. However, in typical Miller style, she chooses to photograph the scene with a Surrealist edge.

artworks.title: Photograph by Lee Miller, 'Picnic:  Nusch and Paul  Éluard, Roland Penrose, Man Ray and Ady Fidelin, Île de  Sainte-Marquerite, Cannes, France, 1937', from the  portfolio 'Quintessential Lee Miller: Six photographs by  Lee Miller'
artworks.medium: Gelatin silver print on Forte Polywarmtone FB semimatt fibrebase paper, hand printed from Lee Miller's original negatives and selenium-toned.
artworks.description:
Photograph by Lee Miller, 'Picnic:  Nusch and Paul Éluard, Roland Penrose, Man Ray and Ady Fidelin, Île de Sainte-Marquerite, Cannes, France, 1937', from the portfolio 'Quintessential Lee Miller: Six photographs by Lee Miller selected by Mark Haworth-Booth', gelatin silver print, 1937, reprinted 2007

Lee Miller met the British Surrealist artist and poet Roland Penrose in 1937. This photograph is taken on holiday with their friends - Nusch and Paul Ėluard, Man Ray and Ady Fidelin - at Mougins in the South of France. Miller and Penrose would continue to host and entertain a variety of artist friends when they moved to Farleys House, a farm in the British countryside.

artworks.title: 'Exploding Hand', from the portfolio 'Quintessential Lee Miller: Six photographs by Lee Miller'
artworks.medium: Gelatin silver print on Forte Polywarmtone FB semimatt fibrebase paper, hand printed from Lee Miller's original negatives and selenium-toned.
artworks.description:
Photograph by Lee Miller, 'Exploding Hand', from the portfolio 'Quintessential Lee Miller: Six photographs by Lee Miller selected by Mark Haworth-Booth', gelatin silver print, c. 1930, reprinted 2007.

In this photograph, an elegant hand reaches towards a door handle seemingly in a cloud of 'smoke'. On closer inspection, these are merely scratches on the glass door of the famous Parisian parfumerie, Guerlain, caused by the diamond rings of the shop's clientele. One of Lee Miller's best known Surrealist images, curator Mark Haworth-Booth believes that it acheives the 'convulsive beauty' which the artist André Breton identified as the hallmark of Surrealist art.
